title: Russia’s AI Law Puts Control Ahead of Capability
key_facts: Russia's law 'On Support for the Development of AI Technologies in the Russian Federation' was signed by President Putin on 26 Jul 2026 and took effect on 1 Sep 2026; several major provisions start on 1 Mar 2027.
It covers 'large foundation models', defined as models with at least 1 billion parameters, including foreign models offered to users in Russia.

It creates 'sovereign' and 'national' model statuses; requirements include a Russian developer, answers generated and stored in Russian-owned data centres in Russia, and conformity with Russian law and 'traditional Russian spiritual and moral values'.
Status holders get state support, a role in shaping AI policy and access to state datasets (subject to FSB agreement); the government can reserve some uses to such models.

From 1 Mar 2027, short-term copying of lawfully obtained or publicly accessible works to train a sovereign or national model is not treated as infringement; the author says this exemption may still be narrowed.
AI services such as chatbots fall under rules requiring user messages to be stored in Russia and the FSB to be given access.
The law is 13 articles long and leaves key details (status criteria, the conformity check, data access) to government rules not yet adopted.
The author argues the law puts control ahead of capability, since Russian models lean on Chinese open models and foreign hardware.
quote_evidence: The law does less to manage the risks of AI than to establish a framework for supporting and controlling developers of large foundation models.
The resolution has not yet been adopted.
Several major provisions take effect March 1, 2027, including the rules governing sovereign and national models, developer obligations, AI-content notices and the copyright provisions.
why_it_matters_hint: Russia ties state support and protected markets for AI model builders to ownership, data location and conformity with state values.
event_date: Signed 26 Jul 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026; main provisions 1 Mar 2027
notes: Read in full from the main session's saved text. This is an analysis piece, so the interpretations (e.g. that 'national' status is a route to build on Chinese open models, or that Russia is exporting a model of control) are the author's reading. Older news re-dated: the law was signed 26 Jul 2026 and the piece says it took effect 'this month' (September).
